newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks down, market poised for recovery.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks down, market poised for recovery.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly lower in lacklustre trade on Friday but traders said the market was poised for recovery after a bearish period.
"Interest of buyers is growing, as their confidence is returning," said Marijana Reskovac of Karlovacka Banka.
Privatisation Minister Ivan Penic on Friday tried to reassure investors that any securities bought bona fide on the secondary capital market would not be challenged.
Shares worth 300 million German marks, purchased at a discount in employee buyouts, were found to be bought illegally as subscribers exceeded a 20,000-mark limit per person.
Of 10 active issues, two were up, six were down and two remained flat.

Drugs firm Pliva, selling 43 shares, lost 200 kuna to 13,500 after hitting an all time high of 13,700 kuna on Thursday. But traders deemed today's decline to be insignificant, and predicted further growth for the blue chip.
Another leading issue, Zagrebacka Banka, lost 16 kuna to 999 on meagre volume of 227 shares. Bank's E-series stayed unchanged at 420 kuna, with 100 shares sold.
Reskovac said hoteliers, which scored spectacular gains in October only to plunge soon afterwards, are now poised to grow and fluctuate around average prices.
Laguna was the only gainer among four active hoteliers, adding 50 kuna to 1,250 on volume of 147 shares.
Jadranturist and Suncani Hvar lost five kuna each to close at 270 and 65 kuna respectively. Riviera fell 10 kuna to 150, trading 386 shares.
Confectioner Kras was the other of the Friday two gainers, up 10 kuna on volume of 714 shares.
Most actively traded food processor Podravka was on the losing side, edging down nine kuna to 226, with 1,939 units sold.
Turnover further dropped to 2.1 million kuna from 9.1 million. Volume was also down at 4,842 shares from 13,190.
